translatorNotes: Informal du (duzen) used throughout, consistent with the marketing tone across the German site.

FLAG: RFQ term. 'RFQ' was rendered as 'Angebotsanfrage' in running prose per the glossary. The English acronym 'RFQ' itself is not carried in the visible body text (only 'Angebotsanfrage'), though the keyword string keeps 'RFQ-Automatisierung' for search. A German native reviewer should confirm whether the audience expects the English acronym 'RFQ' in parentheses on first use, since it is common in German industrial B2B usage.

Glossary terms applied: quote -> Angebot, estimator -> Kalkulator, shop -> Betrieb/Werkstatt, purchase order -> Bestellung (term did not appear in body), supplier -> Lieferant (term did not appear in body), ERP/MRP/CRM/CPQ/CAD kept as acronyms.
Prices kept exact; '$1,000 and $5,000' rendered as '1.000 und 5.000 US-Dollar' with German thousands separator. 'low hundreds of dollars' rendered as 'niedriger dreistelliger US-Dollar-Bereich'.
Brand/tool names kept literal: n8n, Make, Zapier, Unsplash image URLs unchanged.
No em-dashes used anywhere; commas and rewrites replace the English dashes.
Internal same-site links repointed to /de (services, industries, blog, contact). /privacy, /terms, sitemap, mailto, tel and external URLs left unchanged.
Language switcher rebuilt as three-way with EN + ES links and DE current.
No lead/audit form on this page, so no window.__i18n form block was added.
'You own everything we build' rendered as the fixed glossary phrase 'Dir gehört alles, was wir bauen.'
